title: Group without answer labels
summary: Clustering groups similar inputs without known class labels. Here we check distance to two fixed centres; a real clustering method can learn its centres.
introduction: Clustering groups similar inputs without known class labels. Here we check distance to two fixed centres; a real clustering method can learn its centres. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Clustering groups similar inputs without known class labels. Here we check distance to two fixed centres; a real clustering method can learn its centres.

blocks.code:
centres = [2, 8]
point = 7
distances = [abs(point - centre) for centre in centres]
print(distances.index(min(distances)))
blocks.title: Group without answer labels

blocks.text: The output is 1, the index of centre 8. Distances are 5 and 1. Index 1 means the second centre, not a truth label supplied by a teacher.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Assign point 3 to a centre by hand.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A discovered group does not explain why its members are alike.
